why:
QoS events. rclcpp routes every event through one `set_on_new_qos_event_callback` plus a `QOSEventHandler` waitable the executor polls; ours are named callbacks per event (`on_liveliness_lost`, `on_offered_deadline_missed`, `on_message_lost`) registered on the entity. Constraint: no allocator for a per-event handler object and no wait-set to poll it from -- the C/C++ `(callback, context, entity)` triple lives in nros-c's process-wide `status_event_slots` table (16 registrations shared by C and C++, no allocator) and the backend is handed a generation-tagged slot reference, so a registration that outlives its entity is a no-op (issue 1993; until then the five Tier-1 C/C++ setters were UNSUPPORTED stubs that stored nothing). Whether an event is carried is the backend's answer: Cyclone DDS and zenoh carry all five, XRCE-DDS and uORB none, and there the setter returns UNSUPPORTED. The set of events is the same.

phase-456 W2b: the three setters are `PollSubscription<M>`'s now. They take `storage_`, so the dispatch half never had a subscriber to register an event on — it offered them over 656 zero bytes.
